source: Heit and Rotello (2005) Are there two kinds of reasoning?
finding: Exp 1 (Rips-style task, meaning stripped with letters): deduction instructions gave higher sensitivity than induction instructions. A pure criterion shift predicts equal d'.
numbers: N=40 deduction, 40 induction. Valid-argument 'valid' rate .89 vs 'strong' .93. Invalid-argument rate .22 vs .55. d' 1.68 deduction vs 0.93 induction, t(78)=3.11, p<.01. Instruction x correctness F(1,78)=9.67. zROC slopes .84 vs .60.
quote: a substantial change in d' from induction to deduction would make it difficult to explain deduction and induction as following the same scale
limits: Small stimulus set (8 arguments), equal-variance Gaussian SDT assumed; Hayes 2018 says this assumption is the weak point.
agent_relevance: Asking 'is it valid?' versus 'is it plausible?' changes both the bar and how well the judge separates good from bad arguments. An agent should not treat the two prompts as one dial.

source: Heit and Rotello (2005) Are there two kinds of reasoning?
finding: Exp 2 (category arguments such as birds/robins/penguins) repeated Exp 1: valid-argument endorsement almost equal across instructions, but invalid arguments were accepted far more under induction instructions.
numbers: N=48 per condition, 16 arguments. Correct args: .92 deduction vs .88 induction. Incorrect args: .24 vs .57. Interaction F(1,94)=19.22, p<.001. zROC slopes .82 vs .71. Typicality effect F(1,94)=6.91.
limits: Undergraduates, written questionnaires, one instruction wording each (Rips found his three wordings gave no difference).
agent_relevance: The main cost of a plausibility framing is false acceptance of invalid items (.57 vs .24), not rejection of valid ones. Check validity separately when false acceptance is costly.

source: Heit and Rotello (2005) Are there two kinds of reasoning?
finding: Explains why Rips (2001) crossover could be rescued by a one-scale account: induction subjects may bring extra background knowledge. The authors removed meaning to close that escape route.
numbers: Rips (2001): deduction instructions favoured correct-but-causally-inconsistent arguments; induction favoured incorrect-but-causally-consistent ones. Rips tried three instruction wordings per condition and found no differences.
limits: Rips's crossover is only a rough crossover (see Hayes 2018: valid-unbelievable vs invalid-believable differs a lot under deduction, close to none under induction).
agent_relevance: A model asked to judge plausibility leans on world knowledge. To isolate logic, strip or abstract the content first (abstract-content check).

source: Hayes, Stephens, Ngo, Dunn (2018) The dimensionality of reasoning: inductive and deductive inference can be explained by a single process
finding: Three experiments found classic dissociations under conventional analysis: validity mattered more under deduction, believability more under induction. Yet state-trace analysis (STA) needed only ONE latent dimension in every experiment.
numbers: Exp 1 N=122, Exp 2 N=110, Exp 3 N=122. Conjoint monotonic regression tests: Exp 1 load plot p=.25, capacity plot p=.43; Exp 3 p=.10. 10,000 bootstrap samples, alpha .05. Combined data sets (24 conditions): p=.17 and p=.16.
quote: only a single underlying dimension was required to explain patterns of inductive and deductive judgments
limits: Only causal conditionals (modus ponens vs accepting the consequent). A null STA result is not proof of one process; two latent variables with parallel effects would also look one-dimensional (authors concede this).
agent_relevance: Evidence that the difference between plausibility and validity judging may be a threshold and scaling difference on one evidence scale, not two separate engines.

source: Hayes, Stephens, Ngo, Dunn (2018) The dimensionality of reasoning: inductive and deductive inference can be explained by a single process
finding: Exp 1: concurrent memory load and working memory capacity. Low-capacity people were less sensitive to validity and more sensitive to believability, most under induction instructions. Concurrent load itself had little effect on reasoning.
numbers: N=122. Load check: recall .89 low vs .68 high load, F(1,113)=28.07. Capacity x validity chi2(1)=28.30, p<.001. Three-way capacity x instruction x validity chi2(1)=6.23, p<.01. Footnote, 70%-recall rule: validity gap deduction .59 vs induction .33 (high load), .51 vs .32 (low load).
limits: Load effect appeared only after dropping 29 high-load participants; the kept group had 72% high-capacity people vs 49%, so groups were unbalanced. Visual digit load may have been weak.
agent_relevance: Capacity matters more than momentary load. For an agent, a weaker model (low capacity) leans on plausibility; do not expect a prompt to fix that.

source: Hayes, Stephens, Ngo, Dunn (2018) The dimensionality of reasoning: inductive and deductive inference can be explained by a single process
finding: Exp 2 (verbal count-backward load) again showed no reliable load effect, and again capacity effects; STA again one-dimensional.
numbers: N=110 (106 for load analyses). Validity effect larger under deduction chi2(1)=20.06, p<.001; believability effect larger under induction only marginal, chi2(1)=3.27, p=.07. Valid x believable chi2(1)=15.51. Valid-unbelievable and invalid-believable overlapped on the induction axis, making a stronger STA test.
limits: Both load groups did worse than in Exp 1, so the secondary task was harder; only one heavy load level tried.
agent_relevance: Heavy load lowers validity discrimination in general, not selectively under deduction.

source: Hayes, Stephens, Ngo, Dunn (2018) The dimensionality of reasoning: inductive and deductive inference can be explained by a single process
finding: Exp 3: a 5.5 s deadline cut sensitivity to validity and shifted endorsement rates in opposite directions for induction and deduction, but STA still found one dimension.
numbers: N=122. Deadline set so 80% of 20 pilot people were slower. Validity effect: deduction .27 vs induction .09, chi2(1)=21.15; believability effect: deduction .12 vs induction .23, chi2(1)=10.75. Validity effect unspeeded .25 vs speeded .11, chi2(1)=13.65. CMR test p=.10 (partial-order p=.06).
limits: Partial-order p=.06 is borderline. Only two time levels.
agent_relevance: Time pressure removes validity discrimination first. A tight thinking cap (G11) will cost validity checks before plausibility; give validity checks enough budget.

source: Hayes, Stephens, Ngo, Dunn (2018) The dimensionality of reasoning: inductive and deductive inference can be explained by a single process
finding: Power check: the authors simulated a true two-dimensional structure with the same design and STA rejected one dimension, so the one-dimension result is not simply low power.
numbers: Simulation: 30 participants per cell, 8 conditions, linear additive model; CMR chi=12.78, p<.001. Binomial per-response tests in the real data did not reject: Exp 1 p=.74 and .75, Exp 2 p=.95 and .47, Exp 3 p=.11.
limits: The simulated alternative had load and validity hitting deduction more than induction; other two-process structures (parallel effects) stay invisible.
agent_relevance: Treat 'one process' as best current parsimonious fit, not a proven fact.

source: Hayes, Stephens, Ngo, Dunn (2018) The dimensionality of reasoning: inductive and deductive inference can be explained by a single process
finding: Authors argue the earlier rejection of one-dimension models (Rotello and Heit 2009) rested on strong shape assumptions: Gaussian distributions identical for induction and deduction. Different scaling from strength to endorsement can mimic two processes.
numbers: Stephens et al. 2017 applied STA to a database of 26 earlier studies and found a one-dimension model with two independently placed criteria fit them; a new experiment moved the two criteria in opposite directions using base-rate beliefs.
limits: Review of the authors' own prior work, not independent.
agent_relevance: Validity bar and plausibility bar can each move by base rates. Calibrate each threshold separately and keep priors out of the validity bar.

source: Stephens, Dunn, Hayes (2018) Are there two processes in reasoning? The dimensionality of inductive and deductive inferences (Psychological Review 125, 218-244)
finding: Fitted a large family of signal-detection models to three data sets (including Singmann and Klauer 2011). Almost all rejected, including every 2-dimensional model. The only testable model fitting all three: ONE argument-strength dimension with INDEPENDENT decision criteria for induction and deduction.
numbers: Abstract only, via search snippet. Per-set N and fit statistics not read.
quote: only testable model able to account for all 3 data sets was a model with 1 dimension of argument strength and independent decision criteria
limits: Not opened (paywalled; only the supplement landing page was read). Numbers unverified.
agent_relevance: Two independently movable thresholds on one scale. State which bar is being used.

source: Stephens, Matzke, Hayes (2019) Disappearing dissociations in experimental psychology: state-trace analysis to test for multiple processes
finding: Re-ran dual-process evidence cited by Evans and Stanovich (2013): 16 datasets from 9 papers. Most reported dissociations vanish under state-trace analysis.
numbers: With SD .10 assumed for datasets lacking SDs: 6 of 16 tests significant (37.5%), from De Neys et al. 2005b, Klauer et al. 2000, Roberts and Newton 2001. With SD .20 or .30: none significant. The 3 datasets with known SDs: all non-significant. One dimension not rejected for working memory load (De Neys 2006), span, and cognitive ability (Evans et al. 2010).
quote: many of the dissociations thought to reflect the operation of distinct processes disappear against the stricter criteria of state-trace analysis
limits: Not exhaustive; summary statistics only; parametric bootstrap on assumed SDs; some studies had only four conditions (low power). Includes Wason and conjunction-fallacy tasks, not only validity judgments.
agent_relevance: Many 'System 2 helps' effects are one-dimensional shifts. Do not build separate fast and slow components just because ANOVA shows interactions.

source: Ashby (2019) State-trace analysis misinterpreted and misapplied: Reply to Stephens, Matzke, and Hayes
finding: Main critic of the STA programme. Argues STA was never designed to count systems, a monotonic (null) result favours neither side, and the single-system conclusion was preordained by a parsimony claim.
numbers: Focus is the 63 category-learning studies in 28 articles, not the reasoning database. Claims: none of the 63 studies alone identifies the number of parameters varying; COVIS is more parsimonious by model-selection standards.
quote: They report no evidence that favors a single learning system over multiple systems.
limits: Rebuts the category-learning half; reasoning data not directly re-examined. Stephens, Matzke, Hayes replied in 2020 (snippet only).
agent_relevance: Keep the single-process claim at moderate confidence. Design choices should not depend on it.

source: Lassiter and Goodman (2012) How many kinds of reasoning? Inference, probability, and natural language semantics
finding: Replicated the necessary-versus-plausible sensitivity gap WITHIN subjects by changing one word in the conclusion ('It is necessary/plausible/possible/likely/probable/certain that...'), then explained it with a one-scale probability model.
numbers: 507 recruited on MTurk, 485 native English speakers, 10,185 judgments; 21 arguments each. d' for necessary significantly higher than plausible (p<.05). Model R2: certain .60, likely .55, necessary .57, plausible .42, possible .32, probable .41; split-half R2 .66, .57, .70, .37, .34, .47. Mean pairwise Spearman across modal frames .53 (permutation p<.0001); model-expected range .49-.64.
quote: the difference previously reported can be elicited by a difference of a single modal word
limits: Fit is partial. Model has a free exponent per word, so it is flexible. Only novel biological properties with 'horses' as conclusion; no syllogisms or conditionals. Did not decisively beat two-process view.
agent_relevance: A one-word change in the prompt moves the bar and the sensitivity. Tie the modal word to the check type: 'necessarily follows' for validity, 'likely' for plausibility.

source: Lassiter and Goodman (2012) How many kinds of reasoning? Inference, probability, and natural language semantics
finding: The model predicts that wording matters less for very strong (valid) arguments and more for mid-strength invalid ones; acceptance varied less across valid than across invalid arguments, as predicted.
numbers: Model: P(yes) = Pr(C|P)^lambda_M (1-eps) + eps/2; best-fit noise eps=.12. Table 1 (Rotello and Heit 2009, three-premise): deduction hit .94, false alarm .06, d' 3.31; induction hit .95, false alarm .17, d' 2.56.
limits: Author-proposed model with uncontrolled baseline condition; one argument family.
agent_relevance: Weak and mid-strength arguments are where accept or reject flips with wording. Spend validity-check effort there.

source: Stephens, Dunn, Hayes (2017) A two-step signal detection model of belief bias
finding: Belief bias in syllogisms is a decision-threshold effect: a constant-discriminability model fit as well as the free model; a constant-criterion model fit much worse. Held even when believability varied between groups.
numbers: Exp 1 N=38 (within); Exp 2 N=40 believable, 39 unbelievable (between). Constant discriminability: G2(1)=0.23 p=.63 (Exp 1), 0.001 p=.97 (Exp 2). Constant criterion: G2(1)=47.89 and 77.75, both p<.001. Validity effect eta2 .35 and .40.
limits: Students only; two-step confidence model by the authors; the argument-strength alternative still fits Exp 1 (G2(20)=30.18, p=.07) and cannot be tested in Exp 2; Klauer and Kellen disagree.
agent_relevance: Believability moves the threshold for saying 'valid', not the ability to tell valid from invalid. Put a believability-blind step before the final verdict.

source: Hayes, Heit, Rotello (2014) Memory, reasoning, and categorization: parallels and common mechanisms
finding: Summarises Heit and Rotello's two-dimensional model: induction and deduction weight two orthogonal information sources (roughly logical correctness vs consistency with associative knowledge). Monte Carlo simulations said the one-dimension model missed sensitivity differences and effects of argument length and item similarity.
numbers: Reports deduction ROCs with larger area; data well explained by the two-dimensional model. Authors call the debate unsettled, citing Lassiter and Goodman (2012) and Stephens and Dunn (2013).
quote: It would be premature to think that these results have settled the debate in favor of two-process models of reasoning
limits: Secondary summary by the model's own authors, not an independent test.
agent_relevance: Even proponents of two dimensions describe them as two information sources (logic-like vs similarity-like) mixed by task. Build two checks with different weights.

source: Hayes and Heit (2018) Inductive reasoning 2.0 (WIREs Cognitive Science)
finding: Review: logical validity has a bigger effect on deduction judgments, while argument length and similarity have a bigger effect on induction. STA now allows direct tests, and some one-process versions fit Heit and Rotello's own data too.
numbers: No new numbers.
quote: logical validity itself has a greater effect on deduction judgments, whereas more superficial variables such as similarity and the length
limits: Review, written before the 2018 papers were fully published.
agent_relevance: Plausibility judgments are pulled by surface cues (similarity, number of premises). Do not treat 'more supporting premises' as evidence of validity.

source: Trippas, Verde, Handley (2014) The SDT model of belief bias: complexities, complications, and a new set of indices (fluency experiment)
finding: Cognitive ability raised accuracy and lowered belief-based response bias. A disfluent font lowered accuracy, opposite to the prediction that difficulty would make people more analytic.
numbers: N=76 (38 fluent, 38 disfluent), 64 syllogisms. Disfluent d_a 0.51 (Az 64%) vs fluent 0.92 (Az 74%), F(1,74)=6.22, p=.015, omega2 .078, BF 3.30. Ability on accuracy F(1,72)=21.01, omega2 .23; ability on belief bias F(1,72)=9.59, omega2 .12.
limits: Single university; subgroup follow-ups n=16-22; contradicts Alter et al. 2007; moderate Bayes factors (BF .34 for no bias effect).
agent_relevance: Ability changes sensitivity. Making a task harder to read does not make a reasoner more logical.

source: Trippas, Thompson, Handley (2017) When fast logic meets slow belief: evidence for a parallel-processing model of belief bias
finding: Interference between belief and logic judgments flips direction with problem complexity: logic is not always the slower or weaker route.
numbers: Exp 1 N=43 (conditionals): modus ponens, belief judgments hurt more by conflict (.30 vs .24), p=.02; modus tollens symmetric. Exp 2 N=82 (syllogisms): complex multiple-model problems, conflict hurt logic judgments more (.21 vs .09), p=.03; simple syllogisms symmetric. Logic RT 10,718 ms vs belief 8,217 ms (d=0.42).
quote: the complexity of the relevant problem features determines the nature and degree of interference
limits: Within-subjects (task switching possible); some labels in the text looked swapped against the table; 3-point confidence; complexity defined by mental-model theory.
agent_relevance: On simple problems the logic answer is as automatic as belief, so run the validity check even on easy items. On complex multi-model items the plausibility answer wins unless guarded.

source: Singmann and Kellen (2014) Concerns with the SDT approach to causal conditional reasoning: comment on Trippas et al.
finding: Argues the SDT reading of belief effects (bias, not accuracy) depends on unidentifiable assumptions; mean-strength shifts and criterion shifts trade off.
numbers: Linear aggregate ROCs fit better than curvilinear: G2(3)=7.95 p=.05 (VB/IB), 10.63 p=.01 (VU/IU); curvilinear worst G2(3)=13.51 p<.01. Acceptance rates already show A_MP > A_DA and A_AC < A_MT.
limits: A commentary; Gaussian SDT can fit near-linear ROCs at low performance.
agent_relevance: Do not over-trust a 'bias vs accuracy' split from one measure. Use a held-out or counterexample check for validity.

source: Trippas et al. (2014) Modeling causal conditional reasoning data using SDT: caveats and new insights
finding: Pooled valid vs invalid ROC was linear but affirmation (MP vs AC) and denial (MT vs DA) ROCs were curved; believability moved criteria but not accuracy.
numbers: Pooled linear R2=99.9% (quadratic p=.78). MP/AC: linear R2=96%, quadratic 99.99%, p<.004. MT/DA: linear 98%, quadratic 99.99%, p<.002; MT treated as less valid than AC. N not reported on the page.
limits: Regression R2, not formal SDT fits; no d' or c reported; footnote says a symmetric distribution shift would also fit.
agent_relevance: Modus tollens and denial-type inferences are where plausibility-minded reasoners fail most. Add a counterexample test for negative-form inferences.

source: Stephens, Dunn, Hayes, Kalish (2020) A test of two processes: the effect of training on deductive and inductive reasoning (Cognition 199, 104223)
finding: Direct training test. Logic training aimed at the reflective route; belief training aimed at the intuitive route. Logic training improved discrimination of valid from invalid arguments, with different effects on induction and deduction in Exp 2, but a 1-dimensional signal detection model still fit.
numbers: Abstract and metadata only (search snippet, repository page). Two experiments; factors instructions (between), training block, believability, argument type (within). Raw data on Mendeley (10.17632/s247ywy3j4.1). Effect sizes and N not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: If logic training helps validity discrimination along one scale, a prompt-level coaching step may be enough instead of a separate module. Unverified.

source: Singmann and Klauer (2011) Deductive and inductive conditional inferences: two modes of reasoning (Thinking and Reasoning 17, 247-281)
finding: Crossed deduction vs probabilistic instructions with validity and plausibility, looking for a double dissociation, reported as support for two modes. Stephens et al. reanalysed it: a one-dimension model with two independent criteria still fits.
numbers: Not opened. Hayes 2018 says these data challenged a one-dimension model with FIXED criteria but not one with two independent criteria.
limits: Known only through citing papers; one search summary muddled the direction, the Hayes 2018 text is the one used here.
agent_relevance: The dispute is whether criteria move independently, not only whether there is one scale. Allow the validity and plausibility thresholds to move separately.

source: Rips (2001) Two kinds of reasoning (Psychological Science 12, 129-134)
finding: Original dissociation: deduction instructions favoured valid but causally inconsistent arguments; induction instructions favoured invalid but causally consistent ones. Rips took this as incompatible with a single strength scale.
numbers: Not opened. Hayes 2018: the critical pattern is close to a single dissociation (large valid-unbelievable vs invalid-believable gap for deduction, near zero for induction); a state-trace plot of Rips's data was consistent with one dimension (Stephens 2017).
limits: Abstract and citations only.
agent_relevance: Crossovers are cited more than they hold up. Do not rely on a crossover as proof of separate checks.

source: Heit and Rotello (2010) Relations between inductive reasoning and deductive reasoning (JEP:LMC 36, 805-812)
finding: Extended the Rips design with signal detection: deduction more sensitive to validity, induction more to similarity and length; the two-dimensional model fit and the one-dimension model did not.
numbers: Not opened. Hayes 2018: valid arguments were endorsed more than invalid in both conditions, more strongly in deduction.
limits: Secondary description only. Rejection of one dimension rests on equal-shape Gaussian assumptions that Hayes 2018 contests.
agent_relevance: Same as other Heit and Rotello rows.

source: Dube, Rotello, Heit (2010) Assessing the belief bias effect with ROCs: it's a response bias effect (Psychological Review 117, 831-863)
finding: ROC analysis of syllogisms: believability changes where people place the bar, not their ability to separate valid from invalid. The traditional interaction index is invalid because ROCs are curved.
numbers: Not opened. Described in opened papers (Hayes 2014, Stephens 2017, Trippas 2014).
limits: Contested by Klauer and Kellen (2011); Trippas 2013 saw exceptions for high-ability reasoners.
agent_relevance: Same bar-versus-sensitivity message for plausibility.

source: Howarth, Handley, Walsh (2016) The logic-bias effect: the role of effortful processing in the resolution of belief-logic conflict
finding: Random number generation hurt both validity and believability judgments; belief judgments were less accurate overall and more disrupted by conflict, though in a blocked design load hit logic judgments hardest.
numbers: Not opened; abstract on repository page. Hayes 2018 cites it as showing a load effect larger for deduction than for the plausibility-style judgment.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Even 'just plausibility' judgments cost effort.

source: Cheng et al. (2024) Inductive or deductive? Rethinking the fundamental reasoning abilities of LLMs
finding: Separating induction from deduction in LLMs with code-run application (SolverLearner): GPT-4 inferred rules near perfectly, but zero-shot application of the rule collapsed in counterfactual settings.
numbers: GPT-4 inductive 1.0 on all tested arithmetic bases, word orders and spatial setups; deductive zero-shot base 9 0.697, base 11 0.551, spatial max 0.119, Caesar 0. GPT-3.5 deductive base 9 0.117; inductive base 9 0.462, base 11 0.095. Claude 3 inductive base 8 and 9 = 0 vs deductive 0.710 and 0.185.
limits: Single accuracy values, no variance; no chain of thought; hypothesis space must be constrained; model dependent; 'deductive' here means applying a rule, not judging logical validity.
agent_relevance: Supports G3 and G5: let the model propose the rule, let code apply it. Do not ask the model to both guess and check by itself.

source: arXiv 2510.06700 How language models conflate logical validity with plausibility
finding: In LLMs the internal directions for validity and plausibility are aligned, and the alignment predicts the size of content effects. Chain of thought nearly removes the content effect; adding a task-difference direction cuts it too.
numbers: Qwen2.5-32B zero-shot content effect 0.348 (accuracy 81.62%) vs CoT 0.096 (94.60%); Qwen3-14B 0.213 (86.54%) vs 0.014 (96.70%). Probe cosine validity-plausibility 0.48-0.64 vs 0.10-0.13 for hypernymy. Steering (alpha 1.5): Qwen3-14B content effect 0.213 to 0.043 with accuracy 86.54 to 96.70; Qwen2.5-32B 0.348 to 0.072. Mixed-effects similarity beta .557, p=.017; zero-shot beta .188, p<.001 (57 model-prompt pairs).
limits: Open-weight Qwen and Gemma only, one syllogism set from 10 term triples, last-token activations, hyperparameters tuned on two models, plausibility labels from model predictions, cause untested.
agent_relevance: Matches a one-scale picture with shared evidence for validity and plausibility. Explicit step-by-step working cut content effect about 72% (.348 to .096) and 93% (.213 to .014). Use short explicit validity derivation, not a bare verdict.
